About Abacum
Abacum is the leading Business Planning solution for finance teams to drive performance. By automating reporting, enabling collaboration, and simplifying planning and forecasting, we help finance teams shift from number crunching to driving strategic decisions.
Founded in 2020 by two former CFOs, we’ve grown into a global team of 100+ people across 30+ nationalities. Headquartered in New York, we have offices in Toronto and Barcelona. We’re trusted by industry leaders such as Dish Networks, Strava, BetterUp, Kajabi, JG Wentworth, Abridge, Cortex, and hundreds more.
We have raised over $100m, closing in June 2025 our $60M Series B, led by Scale Venture Partners, with the strong participation of Cathay Innovation, Y Combinator, Atomico, Creandum, and angel operators from Adyen, Zapier, and Twitch.
Our mission is ambitious and we can’t do it alone - join Abacum as we build the future of Business Planning!
About the Role
Partners are one of Abacum's fastest-growing areas of growth and we’re investing to make them even more strategic.
As a Senior Partner Account Manager, you’ll own a portfolio of our most strategic technology and advisory partners in North America. That includes the ERPs, accounting platforms, and finance-stack companies whose customers are Abacum's best-fit buyers as well as key advisory firms who help customers transform their finance operations. You’ll turn our partner relationships into repeatable, measurable pipeline and successful joint customers.
This is a senior individual contributor role on the Partnerships team, working closely with Sales, Marketing, Product, and our Partner Solutions team.
What you will do
 Own a portfolio of technology and advisory partners across North America, from recruitment and contracting through activation, GTM execution, growth, and executive-level relationship management.
 Build and maintain joint business plans with each partner. Each plan will cover the shared ICP, target accounts, pipeline, ARR, and services goals, and an operating cadence to hold both sides accountable.
 Drive partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline by co-selling with our AEs through joint account mapping, target-account planning, shared pipeline reviews, and multithreaded relationships on both sides.
 Drive the enablement of partner sales and technical teams on Abacum's value, positioning, and core use cases, in collaboration with Partner Solutions, so their teams can confidently identify, refer, and support opportunities.
 Enable Abacum's AEs to sell with partners: when to engage them, how to run a co-sell motion, and how to jointly manage sales cycles and build field relationships for mutual benefit.
 Partner with Marketing on joint go-to-market programs such as webinars, events, co-branded content, integration marketing, and targeted campaigns with partners.
 Help shape how Partner Operations and the Abacum Partner Program scales, including tiering, incentives, playbooks, reporting, and the processes that make partner-led growth repeatable.
 Work with Product and Partner Solutions on integration roadmaps and joint value propositions and bring partner and market feedback back into the business.
What You Bring
 8+ years in partner management, channel sales, alliances, or business development at a B2B SaaS company managing systems integrators, advisory firms, or consulting partners, including 4+ years in a pipeline- or revenue-accountable partner role.
 A track record of turning technology and advisory partnerships into sourced pipeline and closed revenue, not just integrations, logos, and press releases. Partnerships with ERP, accounting, HRIS, or other Office of the CFO platforms as well as FP&A advisory and system integrators are ideal.
 Experience in the CPM, EPM, or FP&A software space, or selling to finance leaders, is strongly preferred. Strong EPM sales experience without partner experience will also be considered.
 Proven success co-selling alongside AEs on complex, multi-stakeholder mid-market and enterprise deals.
 Confidence building and presenting joint business plans to partner executives and holding partners accountable to their commitments.
 Excellent relationship-building, communication, and negotiation skills, and you’re comfortable in the room with partner leadership and CFOs.
 An analytical, operationally rigorous approach. You’re fluent in Salesforce, partner attribution, and pipeline metrics. Experience with PRM tools is a plus.
 Based in the US and able to travel for partner meetings, prospect meetings, and industry events.
Benefits
 Competitive compensation including equity package
 Competitive vacation policy
 Medical Insurance
 L&D budget
 Access to Meditopia (wellbeing platform)
 Language courses (English / Spanish)

Building on Abacum Intelligence, Abacum Launches Modeler and Brings Agentic Modeling to Every Finance Team

The AI-native FP&A platform brings expert-grade modeling to every finance team. Describe the plan in natural language, and Modeler builds it on live company data in minutes, calculated by Abacum's Engine and approved by finance.
NEW YORK and BARCELONA, Spain, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Abacum, the AI-native FP&A platform, today launched Modeler, an AI agent that brings Agentic Modeling to finance teams. Starting from natural language prompts or existing spreadsheets, Modeler transforms initial inputs into live, fully functional business models instantly ready for execution.
Agentic Modeling is a new approach in which finance defines what a model needs to do, and an AI agent builds it. Instead of building a model line by line, teams set the requirements and the agent does the work. It selects the right structure from proven model blueprints, maps it to the company's connected data and lays out the full logic for review. Work that has traditionally taken days or weeks of manual build now takes minutes, and the time it gives back goes where finance teams want it: analysis, scenarios and strategic decisions.
That time matters. Building and maintaining models is one of the most time-intensive parts of the finance function, and in most companies the models that do exist live with one or two people. When those people are busy, the business waits. When they move on, every model they own is one resignation away from nobody understanding it. Modeler is built to change both.
How Agentic Modeling Works
 Build live models in minutes – ask for the model you need, such as "Build me a P&L from my GL data." Modeler scans the company's connected datasets and builds a working model with calculations across actuals and planning versions, ready to plan from day one.
 Bring what you've built – upload an Excel file and Modeler reads its lines, sections and totals, then rebuilds that model on the data already connected to Abacum, so teams don't start from scratch.
 Approve every plan – before anything is built, Modeler shows the full proposal, variable by variable, with the logic behind each one. Teams refine it in natural language, then approve or reject it. Nothing is saved without approval.
 Trust the math – Modeler proposes the structure and logic; Abacum's deterministic calculation Engine performs every calculation, exactly as it does for models built by hand.
 Explain any model – ask any model to explain its own logic, line by line: what each variable is, how they connect and how every number is calculated. New team members get up to speed without reverse-engineering someone else's work.
 Grow any model – add variables, and add, edit or remove sections in existing models, just by asking.
Time back for the work that matters
With Modeler, the hours that used to go into building go into using the model. A headcount plan the VP of Finance needs by Friday is ready the same morning. A new revenue model for the board starts as a request, not a blank canvas. A question about how a forecast is calculated gets answered on the spot, without waiting for the one person who built it. Finance teams move faster, and the expertise stays with the team.
Commenting on the launch of Modeler, Julio Martínez, Co-Founder and CEO of Abacum, said: "Finance has been told to do more with less for as long as anyone can remember. We think that promise has run its course. Modeler is about doing more with more: more models, built in minutes instead of weeks, by more of the team, with less lift than it has ever taken. The agent does the building, Abacum's Engine still does the math, and finance still approves every model. What changes is how fast you get there, and who gets to build."
Martínez continues: "Every finance leader knows the model that lives in one person's head. That isn't a modeling problem, it's a resilience problem. When more of the team can ask for a model, see exactly how it works, refine it with natural language, and ask it to explain itself, the model belongs to the business. That's what AI-native should mean: not AI bolted onto the side of a platform, but a finance team that is AI-native itself."
What's next
Modeler is the first step in Abacum's agentic modeling roadmap. Later this year, it will bring complete workbooks into Abacum, including formulas and multi-tab files, and will extend editing deeper into existing models, so teams can refine what they've built as easily as they create it.
Availability
Modeler is available today to all Abacum customers as standard functionality, included in the Abacum platform at no additional cost. To see Modeler in action, visit .
About Abacum
Abacum is the AI-native business planning platform. Built first for finance and extended to every department, Abacum holds a company's data, business logic and context in one governed layer, where AI agents and teams plan the business together. Agents own the recurring workflows; people own the judgment. More than 500 customers in over 40 countries run their planning on Abacum, including DISH, ThoughtSpot, Strava, Acorns and Replit. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in New York, with offices in Toronto, Barcelona, Buenos Aires and the UK, Abacum is backed by more than $100 million from investors including Scale Venture Partners, Atomico and Y Combinator. Quick Summary
AccountsIQ and Abacum have formed a strategic partnership to provide mid-market businesses with an integrated AI-powered finance stack. By combining cloud accounting with advanced FP&A tools, the collaboration eliminates manual spreadsheets, enabling automated real-time financial forecasting and multi-entity consolidation for over 35,000 global users.
How Does the AccountsIQ and Abacum Partnership Benefit Finance Teams?
The integration of AccountsIQ and Abacum addresses the critical need for automated data flows in mid-market organizations. By linking multi-currency cloud accounting directly to an AI-native FP&A platform, finance professionals can transition from simple record-keeping to strategic business planning without the risk of manual entry errors. Key benefits include:
   Automated reporting that replaces traditional, error-prone spreadsheets.
   Real-time decision-making powered by actuals flowing directly from accounting to planning modules.
   Multi-entity consolidation with built-in FX conversion for international operations.
This AI-powered finance stack allows teams to focus on high-value analysis rather than data gathering, significantly reducing the time spent on monthly reporting cycles.
Image 7: Singapore Fintech Festival 2026
What Results Has This Integrated Technology Delivered?
Early adoption by firms like investment bank GP Bullhound demonstrates the practical impact of this cloud accounting integration. The bank utilized a custom connector to manage its multi-entry structure, replacing manual uploads with automated synchronization. The partnership leverages Abacum's platform, which has secured $90 million in funding, to serve customers across more than 30 countries. AccountsIQ brings a robust infrastructure supporting 35,000+ users and 30+ technology integrations, ensuring that financial intelligence is scalable for high-growth companies.
How Does This Move the Needle for AI-Powered Finance?
The shift from backward-looking reporting to forward-looking strategic planning is the core value proposition of this alliance. By acting as an intelligence layer, Abacum transforms raw data from AccountsIQ into actionable insights. This partnership is specifically designed for modern European businesses looking to scale with confidence by utilizing clean, consolidated numbers across complex global operations.
FF NEWS TAKE:
This partnership definitely moves the needle for the mid-market. While enterprise-level firms have long enjoyed integrated AI-powered finance stack solutions, mid-market players have often been stuck between basic accounting software and manual spreadsheets. By bridging the gap between cloud accounting and sophisticated FP&A, AccountsIQ and Abacum are democratizing high-end financial intelligence, making real-time financial forecasting a standard requirement rather than a luxury for growing businesses.

AccountsIQ, a cloud accounting platform built for mid-market organisations, has entered into a strategic partnership with Abacum, an AI-native financial planning and analysis provider, in a move designed to give finance teams a fully connected stack spanning accounting through to strategic planning.
Under the new arrangement, finance teams using AccountsIQ will gain direct access to Abacum’s planning, budgeting and forecasting tools, allowing them to progress from verified financial data to advanced analysis without relying on spreadsheets or manual data transfers.
AccountsIQ will continue to handle multi-entity, multi-currency accounting, while Abacum layers AI-driven planning and forecasting capability on top, joining the two into a single workflow that runs from initial recordkeeping through reporting and into forward planning.
The companies said the combined offering is intended to give finance teams more certainty in their figures while freeing up time for teams to take on a more strategic role within their organisations.
As part of the tie-up, Abacum will function as an intelligence layer sitting above AccountsIQ’s data, linking financial information across systems in real time. The two firms describe the partnership as part of a broader shift within European finance functions, away from historical reporting and towards forward-looking planning supported by AI.
Abacum brings together planning, forecasting and reporting within a single collaborative workspace, with a focus on automating reporting tasks, improving forecasting accuracy and supporting collaborative headcount planning. The company has raised more than $90m to date and counts customers in over 30 countries.
AccountsIQ, for its part, is designed specifically for multi-entity, mid-market businesses, supporting more than 35,000 users across upwards of 85 countries, alongside more than 30 technology partner integrations and native multi-entity consolidation with built-in foreign exchange conversion across currencies including GBP, USD and EUR.
Investment bank GP Bullhound is already using the combined platform, with AccountsIQ’s integrations team having built a dedicated Abacum connector to suit the bank’s multi-entity structure, replacing what had previously been a manual upload process with automated data flows.
Abacum partnerships manager TJ Dhadwar said, “At Abacum, we focus on turning financial data into real-time decision-making by replacing spreadsheets with scalable planning and empowering finance teams to lead businesses. Our new strategic partnership with AccountsIQ is the next step in creating a unified finance workflow from record to report to plan, with actuals flowing automatically from AccountsIQ into our platform, removing the manual export/import step that usually breaks FP&A workflows.”
AccountsIQ CEO Darren Cran said, “Our partnership with Abacum comes at the height of the AI-powered finance evolution in the UK and has extended AccountsIQ’s value beyond accounting to support strategic planning and better business decision-making.”
He added, “With Abacum, we have established a partner ecosystem delivering a best-in-class finance stack. Following this new partnership, we plan to continue to help international businesses such as GP Bullhound get clean, consolidated numbers out of complex, multi-entity operations and get those numbers into the hands of FP&A faster.”
